transcription: Main article text only (site header and mega-menu, the breadcrumb with 'Completed / By Water Science School / June 7, 2018', the 'Surface Water Data for the Nation' promo box, the Water Science School topic strip, the 'Education Activities' links, and the related science-topics, multimedia, publications and FAQ widgets and the footer removed). The pull-quote ('"100-year floods can happen 2 years in a row"') and the CoreCast podcast callout ('►► Two 500-Year Floods Within 15 Years? Bob Holmes…') are kept as printed. The recurrence-interval table is kept as pipe-separated rows with its header ('Recurrence interval, years | Annual exceedance probability, percent'). The glossary of flood terms is kept as term/definition paragraph pairs, including the page's own duplicated recurrence-interval paragraph (once after 'Floodplain' ending with a period, once under 'Recurrence interval' ending without one) exactly as served. Superscripts render with ^ (ft^3/s, mi^2). The two charts of dam and urban-development effects are images, not stored; their surrounding text is kept. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: flood probability maths — why a '100-year flood' can happen twice in two years, frequency analysis and recurrence intervals, the worked 1-in-50 rainfall example (6.60 inches in 24 hours = a 50-year recurrence interval) and the 1-in-100 streamflow example (15,000 ft^3/s), the recurrence-interval ↔ annual-exceedance-probability table (250 y = 5% down to 500 y = 0.2%, AEP = 100/T, a 0.2 AEP flood = 20% = 5-year), 1-percent-per-year = 10,000 occurrences per 1 million years, the ten-or-more-years data requirement, and why a 100-year storm does not always cause a 100-year flood. Fits a formula explorer for the AEP ↔ recurrence-interval conversion, a compare table of intervals and probabilities, and quiz cards with predict-then-reveal.
